content.text:
**Resubmitted — IP: deviation (fallback target), minimality defects cured.**

Trimmed from the previous draft, per the verifier:

- **Removed the duplicated Article XXI(b) disapplication** — the standalone "The return and certification obligations in Article XXI(b) do not apply…" sentence is gone; the single named override in the opener carries it.
- **Struck the survival tail** — "and Licensee may retain and continue to use, modify and sublicense the Customization Deliverables and copies thereof after termination" added nothing once the licence is perpetual and irrevocable and Article XXI(a)–(b) are overridden.
- **Removed the off-checklist data carve-out** from the return sentence; element 8 only limits Licensor's licence in our data, which the retained final sentence does.
- **Removed the scope creep** "or under any statement of work or order"; the grant is keyed to the Article VII(b) customization mechanic only, using no undefined terms.
- **Named Article III expressly** in the override so the right to use, modify, sublicense and hold copies of the Customization Deliverables is not left in tension with Article III's retained no-copy sentence.

The clause is now a single sentence of grant plus one sentence of data-licence limitation. Fallback is position-complete; preferred is deliberately not claimed (no assignment of the customizations to us, no affirmative data-ownership sentence), which is stated in the rationale rather than flagged. Licensor's ownership of the Licensed Technology, its enforcement rights, the Article VII(b) pricing mechanic and the rest of Article XXI are untouched. Anchors and minimality validated `ok:true`.
